text:
alex: Ran the 8xA100 TP=2 PP=4 decode-profile this morning. Observed long NCCL stalls during autoregressive steps, looks like KV fetches are triggering cross-TP all-reduces a lot. attaching short summary below.
priya: can you paste the perf counters or the trace snippet? curious about nccl_wait vs compute time.
alex: summary: `nccl_wait_avg=42ms`, `compute_avg=9ms`, `p99_tail_wait=110ms`. trace shows repeated small all-reduces right after KV reads.
mateo: that's...pretty bad. Are KV partitions colocated with the same devices that serve the attention head?
jing: likely not — current sharding puts KV per-tensor-parallel shard which means PP stages request remote KV for some layers, causing syncs.
sam: quick thought: what if we move KV ownership to PP stage that holds those layers (i.e., shard KV by pipeline stage) so fetches are local to PP device?
priya: tradeoff: PP-local KV increases memory per-stage, might exceed per-GPU memory for 30B unless we also DP or quantize more aggressively.
mateo: I ran a synthetic microbench earlier replicating KV access pattern across TP/PP combos. Results: TP-only KV sharding => lower memory but +2.1x all-reduce bytes. PP-local KV => all-reduce drops ~3x but local memory up by ~28%.
alex: also tried hybrid: group GPUs into PP-groups (each group has replicated DP across groups) and TP inside group. Hybrid reduced nccl_wait_avg to 15ms and compute_util stayed ~10ms, so overlap improved. Throughput dropped ~8% vs baseline TP-only due to extra replication.
perf-bot: PERF ALERT: Deploy r456 caused +18% p99 latency for chat-gen on 8x setups (metric: generation.p99.latency).
priya: that matches. hypothesis: small KV fetches serialized NCCL ops preventing compute overlap. Need two things: (1) batching heuristic that coalesces KV fetches per batch to avoid many tiny all-reduces, (2) sharding policy experiment (TP vs PP vs hybrid).
mateo: agreed. Suggested action items: `A) kv-aware-batching heuristic in runtime scheduler (coalesce per-request kv keys into chunked fetches)`, `B) run the hybrid sharding microbench at multiple model sizes (7B/13B/30B)`, `C) add CUPTI/NVML sampling to measure overlap more precisely`, `D) dashboard metric 'kv_cross_group_bytes' and 'nccl_wait_ms_per_step'`.
alex: I'll land a quick profiler that records per-step nccl_wait and KV fetch bytes. command I used for microbench: ```python tools/bench/kv_shard_micro.py --config configs/8xA100-tp2-pp4.yaml --trace nccl,wg```. posting raw traces to #perf-artifacts shortly.
priya: for the heuristic: we can detect high nccl_wait spikes and switch runtime from per-request fetch to batched-prefetch for that conversation id. That should reduce switches mid-conversation.
sam: I'll prototype runtime scheduler changes — plan: implement a KVFetchAggregator that groups keys within a 5ms window and issues one all-reduce/chunked transfer.
jing: watch out for tail-latency regressions for first-token; batching introduces headroom tradeoffs. we need dynamic thresholds.
mateo: also consider quantized KV cache (4-bit) for PP-local to reduce mem overhead and make PP-local feasible for 30B. our quant kernels add ~2ms but avoid network.
alex: timeline: I'll run hybrid microbench today, sam will prototype aggregator, priya will add dashboard metrics, mateo will test quantized KV impact by EOD.
priya: cool. please tag me in traces. I'll correlate with the recent regression and prepare a short doc for the runbook change (fallback to TP-only if memory/cost budget violated).
perf-bot: NOTE: linked perf dashboard -> https://console.redwood/perf/alerts/r456 (read-only).
alex: thanks team. if hybrid shows consistent p99 reductions we should consider defaulting to PP-local KV for PP-heavy topologies. :thumbsup:
